summary: Penobscot County lookout built by the U.S. Forest Service in Pennsylvania, moved to Dixmont in 1940 and removed by the Maine Forest Service in July 2006.

facts.design: Wooden tower with a 14 x 14 live-in cab and catwalk; built by the U.S. Forest Service
facts.status_note: Tower removed July 26, 2006; no source describes the site today

events.note: Maine Forest Service dismantled the Pennsylvania tower and moved it to Harris Mountain, Dixmont; register's Built field gives 1940
1943-44 forest commissioner's report describes a new 41-foot tower begun on Mount Harris in 1944 and due in 1945; sources do not say whether it is the tower removed in 2006
Registered August 7, 1993; nominated by Caroline S. Parmenter, R.N., FFLA
Removed July 26, 2006 by the Maine Forest Service after years of vandalism and deterioration
FFLA helped the Dixmont Historical Society include a section on the lookout in its centennial history book
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

corrections.why: The NHLR Built field gives 1940, but the register text and the Forest Lookouts page say the tower was built by the U.S. Forest Service in Pennsylvania and moved to Harris Mountain by the Maine Forest Service in 1940. The sources give no original build year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR 'Built 1940' entry refers to the year the tower was moved to Harris Mountain. Its original build year is not given in the sources read. The 1944 report about a new Mount Harris tower is not resolved; see notes.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1943-44 forest commissioner's report describing a new 41-foot tower begun on Mount Harris in 1944 and due in 1945. The NHLR and Former Fire Lookout Sites pages say the tower stood in Pennsylvania until 1940 and was moved here. The sources do not say whether the tower removed in 2006 was the 1940 move, the 1944-45 tower, or both. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Maine chapter Facebook post seen only in search results dates the Harris tower to 1945; I could not open it, so it is not cited. The NHLR text gives the tower as 'a 50 wooden tower' with no unit, so no height is recorded. The NHLR 'Staffed? Yes' field is a question on a volunteer visit form, not a staffing history, and I did not use it. No staffing or fire history was found. No source describes the site today.
